newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government buys 5,770T rubber since May 15.
newsitem.headline: Thai government buys 5,770T rubber since May 15.

text.p: Thailand has spent 170 million baht ($6.8 million) buying 5,770 tonnes of rubber under a government intervention scheme to prop up prices since May 15, a senior government official said on Friday.

Chakant Saengraksawong, the director of the Hat Yai rubber auction market, told Reuters that the government expected to spent one billion baht of a four-billion-baht budget earmarked for the scheme to support the price until the end of July.
He stressed that the government will not sell the purchased rubber but would keep it in stock until global prices improved.
"There are all sorts of rumours in the market -- that the government will sell a big amount of rubber to China which is not true," he said.

"Whatever contracts or MOU we have with China is likely to be fulfilled by the private sector. We will not dump the rubber into the market now as it could further pressure prices. Otherwise, why would we start the programme in the first place if not to prop up local prices," the official added.

The government, in a move to calm rubber producers who were disgruntled over bearish prices, last month pledged to buy unsmoked sheet rubber grade three at 29 baht a kg and grade four at 25 baht a kg.
However, Chakant said the government is expected to use only one billion baht for the scheme and not all four billion baht.
"We hope that the prices will soon recover to the point that we do not have to intervene. Moreover, the amount of unsmoked sheet grade three supplies is also limited," he added.
Chakant said that of the total amount of rubber the government bought under the intervention plan, more than 60 percent were grade three.
